- Model consistently overestimates prices in the short term (1-3 days) after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive or neutral.  
- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.5), model tends to underestimate downward momentum; adjust forecast downward by 1-2% of recent range.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct — reduce forecast by 3-5% in next 3-5 days.  
- Mean reversion is strong in 10-14 day horizons; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1-2% per day until convergence.  
- If sentiment is positive and price is falling, model often ignores sentiment — if sentiment > 0.5, increase forecast by 0.5-1% to reflect bullish bias.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model is prone to “late correction” — if true outcome is below 30-day moving average, reduce forecast by 1-3% for next 5 days.  
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile, model tends to over-smooth — use 7-day weighted average for smoothing instead of 18-day.
